qualifications: The all-case goal remains open. Latest complete sweep measured 1,388 passes, 675 skips, 2,548 failures, 116 timeouts, and no crashes across 4,727. Focused outcomes do not establish a new full-suite total.

Recursive tree ownership is one private class-data Map in the VM heap. Each record holds stats, child watcher, and symbolic classification; callback cycles remain visible to GC. Canonical per-path watchers own kernel lifetime, and public watch/stat/readdir overrides retain original effects and errors. No parallel native root map or phantom work is introduced.

Rust owns directory discovery, relative names, ignored-subtree exclusion, file changes, subtree deletion, synchronous one-shot close, private class-data initialization, and iterator event/abort policy. Thin checked class/function facades provide presentation and shared-language async-generator delegation. The pinned recursive ref/unref methods return undefined and leave ordinary stat records unchanged.

Recursive fs.promises.watch forwards to the iterator with lazy validation through the shared async-generator protocol. Tested iterator results have Node null prototypes, pending next calls retain event resolvers, closure returns completion, and original abort causes are preserved. Nonrecursive promise watching, full queue/overflow policy and propagation flags remain open.

Supporting fixes share the Rust glob compiler for zero-segment globstar prefixes, existing filesystem remove operation for callback fs.rm, canonical event constructor for the internal binding, and URL state WeakMap for internal URL conversion branding. The private URL namespace is cached separately and does not add the conversion helper to public URL exports.

Eight new Node oracles cover public per-path hooks and class reflection, synchronous close/reference projection, discovery and ignore behavior, root/nested globstar matches, asynchronous removal and errors, iterator/GC safety, recursive promise event and abort causes, and internal URL identity/brands. The first URL oracle unnecessarily imported an unavailable source module from the unit-test default library; its native-helper contract was corrected, while the actual upstream deletion-race fixture verifies source integration.

Initial watch subset reached 33/37. Globstar, callback rm and recursive promise watch fixes reached 36/37. The internal deletion race first failed at missing FSEvent; after exposing that constructor, it reached missing toPathIfFileURL. The internal helper fix established all 37/37 with twenty gains and no lost passes. Final group evidence contains actual integrated outcomes.

Before source publication, integrated four upstream Wasm/shared-core commits ending at 94b36323e, including accumulator-carried dispatch heads, retrained link orders, and unconditional-jump dispatch copies. The draft was parked/reapplied cleanly, workspace/runtime/API/framework/group checks rerun, and the shared active-program/call-root guard invariant preserved.

Complete private handle/start/wrap metadata, reflection/proxy details, advanced globs, nonrecursive promise watches, queue/overflow and abort propagation policy, callback removal retry/options/error policy and Buffer/URL paths, ordinary stat decorators/Temporal, and major transport/IPC/Worker/HTTP2 gaps remain open.

Groups and measurements ran sequentially without overlapping compilation or additional guest checks. Frozen sibling hashes and source provenance are retained; compiled runner metadata may identify the parent merge before source commit. Baseline and candidate also differ by the integrated shared dispatch commits.

All eight fixed-work fixtures and Richards are iteration diagnostics, one round with no matched production qualification or speed claim. Hardware instruction/cycle counters remain unavailable on this host (previous perf_event_open ENOENT); no substitutes. Empty-script samples retain actual wait4 RSS and alternating order.
